title: Windows Development Environment & Professional Tooling
outcome: Build and verify a reproducible Windows development environment without relying on hidden machine state.
artifact: A verified toolchain report showing shell, Git, Node, Corepack/pnpm, editor, PATH, ports, and diagnostic commands.
labSteps: Open ordinary PowerShell and record pwd, whoami, and PATH-related observations.
Install or verify Git and VS Code with user-level installation where possible.
Install the course Node line with a version manager and prove which executable is active.
Enable Corepack and activate the repository package-manager version.
Verify git, node, npm/corepack, pnpm, and editor command availability from a fresh terminal.
Deliberately create a PATH or port conflict in a safe sandbox and diagnose it with Get-Command/Get-NetTCPConnection.
failureModes: Terminal still using an old executable after installation
EPERM caused by writing to protected locations
Different shells resolving different PATH values
Port already in use by a forgotten development process
mastery: Can prove which executable a command resolves to
Can explain user PATH vs system PATH
Can identify a process occupying a port
Can recreate the toolchain on another machine from notes
principles: Verify tools from the terminal instead of assuming an installer succeeded.
Understand PATH, ports, processes, shells, and working directories because they explain many setup failures.
Prefer user-level development tooling when administrator privileges are unnecessary.
Record exact versions and verification commands so another developer can reproduce the environment.
